prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire graphene, without prejudice to the origin of the superconductivity

statement.case_for: I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my preferred single-part prize. The scientific content has not been challenged in round 1: a quantitative continuum-model prediction in 2011 that flat bands appear near a specific twist angle, and a 2018 experimental discovery at that angle of correlated insulators and superconductivity, since reproduced independently in many laboratories and extended to other graphene and moire heterostructures. The central lesson, that band width can be tuned against interaction strength with a twist angle, is robust whatever the pairing mechanism turns out to be, and that is what the citation rewards. Credit among the supplied names is also clean, with two theorists for the prediction and one experimentalist for the discovery. After reading the other seven statements I have not moved, but I have dropped my earlier remark that I could accept B002 as the second part of a two-part prize: with a three-person limit across the whole configuration, a Katori-Ye part plus a B038 part would need five names and cannot be proposed honestly. I also accept that the committee majority around B002 rests on real strengths, and I keep it as my first alternative.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains timing. The field is about eight years old, the pairing mechanism and several correlated phases are unresolved, and a prize now could be read as early. Experimental credit is a second weakness: Cao and the other first-paper authors did much of the bench work and sit outside three names, and the supplied set does not recognise earlier twisted-bilayer and moire experiments or the many later theory papers. The 2010 graphene and 2016 topology prizes also make condensed matter somewhat crowded. By contrast, B002 is more mature and is credibly attributed to two people, and I recognise that a committee that weighs maturity above conceptual breadth would reasonably place it first.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks should be first because the magic-wavelength lattice concept and the 10^-18 realisation are mature, reproduced and cleanly credited to Katori and Ye.
responses.response: I accept the maturity and the two-name credit and do not dispute either. On the chair's first question, the honest answer is that the citation recognises the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice, which allows many atoms to be interrogated at once with the light shift cancelled; the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes recognised the counting machinery and single-particle control, not that route to stability. That is a real distinction, but it is a distinction in method within a recognised line, and the discovery content is smaller than what moire flat bands added to condensed matter. I therefore keep B002 as my first alternative and not my first choice, and I do not think your own boundary question about Boulder affects the science.

responses.point: Credit for B002 is the most compact on the shortlist, but the lattice proposal and the long JILA programme, with Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Derevianko, make the split between Katori and Ye contestable.
responses.response: This is the real weakness of B002 and it is similar in kind to my own difficulty over Cao in B038, so I will not use it against you more than against myself. In both cases the three or two supplied names are defensible as concept plus decisive realisation, and neither fully covers the experimental group effort. The difference is that B002 has a long record and a Katori-Ye allocation that colleagues in the field have used consistently, whereas in B038 the experimental allocation to Jarillo-Herrero alone is more exposed. I would like to hear from you whether waiting for the redefinition of the second would, in your view, resolve the credit question or just postpone it.

responses.point: B038 needs a citation that does not claim an explanation of the superconductivity, and the committee risks rewarding a platform before its central physical lesson is known.
responses.response: I agree with the wording point and have added to my citation that it is without prejudice to the origin of the superconductivity. On the platform objection, I would say the central lesson is already known and is the flat-band and correlation competition, which has been confirmed through STM, transport and compressibility measurements in many groups. Where I would differ slightly from you is on the evidence that would raise maturity: for me it is a reproducible, mechanism-independent consensus on the phase diagram, such as broad agreement on the nature of the correlated insulator at integer filling, rather than a settled pairing theory. If that existed I would call the field mature; I am not sure it exists yet, so we should treat the timing risk as real.

responses.point: B002 is the candidate where science, credit and maturity line up without a trade-off, and B038 is less mature, with circuit QED now second-ranked for you.
responses.response: I accept that B002 has the cleanest alignment, which is why it remains my first alternative. I do not accept that absence of trade-offs is the same as strength of case: the committee still has to choose between a mature refinement and a younger, conceptually more novel result, and I think the latter weighs more at the margin. I also note that your move away from circuit QED and your remark on the 2025 circuit prize are consistent with my own reasoning on B017, so we agree that a second superconducting-circuit prize now would be hard to justify.

responses.point: Six members placed B002 in their top five, so it has the widest support, and a two-laureate prize is natural with no statutory limit forcing a trade-off.
responses.response: I take the breadth of support seriously as evidence that the case is robust across specialties, and I ranked B002 fifth myself. At the same time, I would not treat a count of top-five placements as a substitute for scientific judgment, as the protocol says, and the placements are weighted by caution as much as by enthusiasm. B038 is the most frequent alternative of the five, which suggests it is the common second choice. If the committee settles on B002, I would not object, and I would ask only that the citation stay anchored in the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated states as sufficient without a settled superconducting mechanism.
Whether naming only Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero fairly reflects Cao and the other early experimental authors, and earlier twisted-bilayer theory and moire experiments.
Whether thematic overlap with the 2010 graphene and 2016 topology prizes weighs against B038 and B015 in condensed matter.
Whether a prize for B002 before the redefinition of the second would be judged early or timely.
statement.conflict_note: No documented conflict. My research in electronic-structure theory and two-dimensional materials is close to the subject of B038 and B015, but I have no documented personal, collaborative or institutional link with any credited person on the shortlist. Unlike Kroll, Johansson and Olsson, I have no disclosure to update for B002, B017 or B055.
